title: Finite coefficient comparison for supported lattice Hom
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$ and all morphisms are over $k$. On each small pro-étale site put $R_Y=p_Y^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, $A_n=\mathcal O_E/(\pi_E^n)$ and $A_{n,Y}=p_Y^*\underline{A_n}$ for $n\ge1$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-sfb-torsion-stratum-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], in universes making these sites small [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $\operatorname{Res}_n:D(A_{n,X})\to D(R_X)$ for termwise restriction along the quotient coefficient morphism [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be closed, $j:V\hookrightarrow X$ its open complement, $u:S\hookrightarrow Z$ open and $a=i\circ u$. Use $a_!=i_*u_!$, closed module direct image after open module extension by zero [def-sfb-module-lower-star, def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. Let $L_0$ be a lisse $R_S$-module, meaning pro-étale locally finite free, and put $Q=a_!L_0$ and $L_0^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{R_S}(L_0,R_S)$ [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Use the derived support functor $R\underline\Gamma_{Z,R}$ and global derived Hom of [sk-lem-formal-closed-support], the ordinary derived tensor of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], and derived global sections $R\Gamma$ [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology].

Fix $n\ge1$ and any $\overline K\in D(A_{n,X})$. The ring $A_n$ is finite and killed by a power of $\ell$. The reduced lattice $L_{0,n}=L_0/\pi_E^n$ is finite locally free over $A_{n,S}$, its dual has the canonical evaluation-compatible identification
$$\mathcal Hom_{A_{n,S}}(L_{0,n},A_{n,S})\simeq L_0^\vee/\pi_E^n,$$
and the derived source reduction is $Q\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{R_X}A_{n,X}\simeq a_!L_{0,n}$ in $D(A_{n,X})$. For every integer $q$ there are isomorphisms of abelian groups, natural in $\overline K$,
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R_X)}(Q,\operatorname{Res}_n\overline K[q])
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_{n,X})}(Q\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{R_X}A_{n,X},\overline K[q])\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_{n,X})}(a_!L_{0,n},\overline K[q])\\
&\cong H^qR\Gamma\bigl(S,(L_0^\vee/\pi_E^n)\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{A_{n,S}}u^*R\underline\Gamma_{Z,A_n}\overline K\bigr).
\end{aligned}$$
Here $R\underline\Gamma_{Z,A_n}$ is the support functor in the finite coefficient category, defined by $M\mapsto i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ and total right derivation. The last tensor may equally be computed by ordinary termwise tensor with the finite locally free reduced dual. The first comparison is the derived extension/restriction scalar adjunction; no flatness of $R_X\to A_{n,X}$ is assumed.

proof.text: The coefficient datum gives a discrete valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ with finite residue field and uniformizer $\pi_E$. Apply [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] to obtain finiteness of $A_n$. For the torsion assertion, $|\ell|_E=|\ell|_\ell=\ell^{-1}<1$ by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], so $\ell\in\mathfrak m_E=(\pi_E)$. Write $\ell=\pi_E c$ with $c\in\mathcal O_E$. Then $\ell^n=\pi_E^n c^n$ annihilates $A_n$. Thus $A_n$ is an admissible finite coefficient ring; no unramifiedness assertion is needed.

source.place: Torsion targets: admissibility of the finite quotient; elementary ideal calculation from the stated coefficient datum.

proof.text: By [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution], $0\to R_Y\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}R_Y\to A_{n,Y}\to0$ is exact for every $Y$. Thus the coefficient sheaf in the question is the actual quotient $R_Y/\pi_E^nR_Y$. On a slice trivializing $L_0$ with rank $r$, its quotient is $A_{n,S}^{\oplus r}$, with the quotient action. These local descriptions prove that $L_{0,n}$ is finite locally free. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-free-derived-scalars] with $R=R_S$, $B=A_{n,S}$ and $M=L_0$: $L_0$ is flat and K-flat in degree zero and the canonical scalar-extension comparison gives $A_{n,S}\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{R_S}L_0\simeq L_{0,n}$ in $D(A_{n,S})$. This application imposes no flatness on the quotient ring.

source.place: On X: exact quotient resolution; local finite-free specialization of the derived scalar comparison, as used in Lattices of the item source.

proof.text: Define $L_0^\vee/\pi_E^n\to\mathcal Hom_{A_{n,S}}(L_{0,n},A_{n,S})$ by $\overline\lambda(\overline x)=\overline{\lambda(x)}$. Changing $x$ or $\lambda$ by a multiple of $\pi_E^n$ changes the value by such a multiple, so the map is well-defined. On a slice with a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ it sends the reductions of the coordinate functionals to the coordinate functionals of $A_{n,S}^r$ and is an isomorphism. The formula is independent of this basis, hence gives a global isomorphism, with inverse the identification in the question. Its displayed formula proves compatibility with evaluation. In particular both $L_0^\vee$ and its reduction are locally finite free, also for rank zero.

source.place: Torsion targets: the reduced dual L_0^vee/pi_E^n; local coordinate evaluation calculation.

proof.text: Put $T_n=\operatorname{Res}_n(Q\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{R_X}A_{n,X})$. In the integral derived category, [det-lem-int-tensor-projection] with $M=L_0$ and $L=A_{n,X}$ gives $T_n\simeq a_!(L_0\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{R_S}a^*A_{n,X})$. Here $a^*A_{n,X}=A_{n,S}$ by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. The comparison of step 2 identifies the right side with $a_!\operatorname{Res}_n L_{0,n}$ in $D(R_X)$. In passing between extension and underlying tensor we use the chain isomorphism $\nu$ of [lem-sfb-slice-scalar-hom-chain-adjunction] on a K-flat resolution: termwise scalar extension, followed by restriction, is the underlying $R$-linear tensor. The projection-formula node also states that $u_!$ and $i_*$ are exact termwise functors in this setting. Their coefficient actions are the given pulled-back actions, so restricting the finite coefficient action on $i_*u_!L_{0,n}$ gives this same integral object.

source.place: Locally closed immersions: specialize the projection formula to the quotient coefficient module; underlying scalar extension is the normalized termwise tensor.

proof.text: To obtain an isomorphism in $D(A_{n,X})$, use the quotient map $Q\to\operatorname{Res}_n(a_!L_{0,n})$ and take its adjunct $c_n:Q\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{R_X}A_{n,X}\to a_!L_{0,n}$ under [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. This is an actual finite-coefficient morphism. Its underlying map is the quotient augmentation of the cone $[Q\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}Q]$: [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution] computes underlying derived reduction by that cone, and the adjunction's normalized formula $x\otimes a\mapsto a\,\overline x$ gives this augmentation. More explicitly, on a K-flat resolution $P\to Q$ the adjunct is represented by $P\otimes A_{n,X}\to a_!L_{0,n}$ sending $p\otimes a$ to $a\,\overline p$; the comparison with the free two-term quotient resolution has the same quotient augmentation. Multiplication by $\pi_E^n$ is injective on $L_0$, as checked on the local finite free slices in step 2; exactness of $i_*u_!$ in [det-lem-int-tensor-projection] therefore gives $0\to Q\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}Q\to a_!L_{0,n}\to0$ on underlying integral modules. Consequently that augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Restriction of scalars leaves kernels and cokernels unchanged and so detects cohomology isomorphisms; hence $c_n$ is an isomorphism in $D(A_{n,X})$. This proves the source reduction with its finite coefficient action, rather than only an integral isomorphism.

source.place: On X: the two-term quotient resolution and its augmentation; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), normalized scalar adjunct. Coefficient action made explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] to the small site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the quotient map $R_X\to A_{n,X}$, $K=Q$ and $H=\overline K[q]$. This gives the first displayed Hom isomorphism for every $q\in\mathbf Z$: restriction is termwise and commutes with shifts. Precomposition with the inverse of $c_n$ from step 5 gives the second displayed isomorphism. These are isomorphisms of abelian groups: the adjunction on complexes sends $g$ to $(x\otimes a\mapsto a g(x))$ and is additive, and precomposition is additive. Naturality in $\overline K$ follows from the naturality in the target of the cited adjunction.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint, specialized to the identity topos with quotient ring map; the item source Integral targets and sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change use this scalar adjunction.

proof.text: Apply [det-lem-formal-closed-support-stratum] with the admissible coefficient $\Lambda=A_n$, the same factorization $a=i\circ u$, $L=L_{0,n}$ and $K=\overline K$. The finite locally free module of step 2 is finite locally projective, so the cited statement gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_{n,X})}(a_!L_{0,n},\overline K[q])\cong H^qR\Gamma(S,L_{0,n}^\vee\otimes u^*R\underline\Gamma_{Z,A_n}\overline K)$ naturally in $\overline K$. The support functor here has precisely the kernel and right-derived definition in [sk-lem-formal-closed-support]. Substitute the evaluation-compatible identification of step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-free-derived-scalars] to the reduced dual over $A_{n,S}$: it is flat and K-flat in degree zero. Its ordinary termwise tensor with any complex therefore computes its derived tensor. This gives the third displayed comparison and the last tensor assertion. All these statements apply to the ordinary unbounded categories and to arbitrary $\overline K$; no constructibility, boundedness, completeness or flatness of $R_X\to A_{n,X}$ has been introduced.

source.place: First, second and third isomorphisms and the final Hom/cohomology assertion, now with finite coefficient ring A_n; Torsion targets in the item source.
